report_evidence.title: Thin PMMA films
report_evidence.text: A 100 µm film reached a steady spread rate of 2.2 mm/s before flow cutoff. In a separate test, the estimated flow at extinction was about 1.1 cm/s.

report_evidence.title: Nomex samples
report_evidence.text: The three Nomex samples in the report did not ignite.

report_evidence.title: Black PMMA rods
report_evidence.text: Spread was observed at oxygen concentrations as low as 17.5% in microgravity. The normal-gravity comparison observed no spread below 19%.

report_evidence.title: PMMA rod flammability boundary
report_evidence.text: The fitted boundary reached a minimum near 13.5% oxygen for the tested axial stagnation flow configuration.

report_evidence.title: SIBAL fabric across BASS and BASS-II
report_evidence.text: The report gives concurrent-flow quenching speeds of 1–5 cm/s over its tested conditions, with higher quenching speeds at lower oxygen.

report_evidence.title: B1 · Appendix A.1
report_evidence.text: At 22.2% initial oxygen, the flame extinguished after the flow was turned off. Final CO was 6 ppm.

report_evidence.title: B3 · Appendix A.1
report_evidence.text: The calibrated initial oxygen entry is 22.2% and final CO was 19 ppm. The observation notes uncertainty about the starting oxygen.

report_evidence.title: P13a and P13b · Appendix A.3
report_evidence.text: Both tests began at a reported 5 cm/s before flow reduction. Final CO was 450 ppm in P13a and 72 ppm in P13b.

report_evidence.title: T25 and T26 · Appendix A
report_evidence.text: Both tests ignited at 5 cm/s before flow was set to 2.5 cm/s. Final CO was 17 ppm in T25 and 24 ppm in T26.

overall_insights: BASS-II provides microgravity solid-material evidence at ISS cabin conditions. FLEX provides liquid-droplet observations at oxygen and pressure levels closer to the example habitat targets.
The BASS-II report’s black PMMA rod comparison found flame spread down to 17.5% oxygen in microgravity and no spread below 19% in the normal-gravity comparison (PDF page 58).
The selected FLEX runs include disruption and burn-to-completion outcomes. These observations do not locate a flammability boundary or establish the behavior of solid materials.
gaps: No solid-material tests above 22.2% O2 or below ISS cabin pressure.
No partial-gravity (lunar 1/6 g) data in either investigation.
BASS-II flame spread rates are reported at material level in the report, not per test in the table.
FLEX covers liquid droplets only and does not measure flame spread.
caveats: The BASS-II table was transcribed; five final O2 readings are impossible and were ignored, and flow speeds are free text.
FLEX 'Disruption' outcomes are not defined in the report.
The FLEX burning-rate column is labeled 'mm' in the source table. Its physical unit is unconfirmed.
Lunar relevance is inferred from tested conditions; neither investigation names a lunar base.
